title: Aurora Finance - Procurement: MSA/DPA/SLAs/Pricing Onboarding
summary: Procurement kickoff to review Redwood MSA/DPA, draft SLAs, pricing approval path, and next steps for vendor onboarding. Legal reviewed data residency, encryption/KMS, and audit logs; procurement clarified procurement timeline and PO process. Redwood to send redlined MSA + DPA and SLA summary; security to provide SOC2 attestation and encryption detail. Pricing approval contingent on committed monthly spend and pilot results.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Ava (Security), Carlos (CS) — Martin (Aurora Procurement), Leila (Legal), Samir (VP Eng), Emily (IT Sec), Rina (DevOps)

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, appreciate it. we're gonna run through the procurement checklist — msa, dpa, slas, pricing and onboarding. if at any point i stumble say jump in.
00:18 Martin: thanks jordan. quick context — we've shortlisted 2 vendors, one is redwood and another is a large provider; procurement wants to make sure legal and security are happy. timeline is end of Q1 for production, so we need approvals by mid-january ideally.
00:35 Leila: and legal will be reviewing the MSA and DPA. we've got a few standard clauses to confirm — data residency, liability caps, and audit rights.
00:48 Jordan: understood, leila. we circulated the standard redwood MSA and DPA last week, i'll send the most recent redlines today. priya, maybe run through the SLA and pilot stuff?
01:05 Priya: yeah sure — so from an SLA perspective we offer tiered uptime guarantees depending on deployment mode. hosted api customers typically see a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA; dedicated gets a 99.95% option with stronger latency targets. we also provide latency SLOs per model class, and we have credit formulas for incidents.
01:35 Samir: can you clarify "latency SLO per model class" — do you mean a contractual latency figure? our app is latency-sensitive; 95th percentile under 200ms is our target.
01:48 Priya: good q. we usually define latency SLOs as a target, not a hard contractual SLA unless it's a dedicated contract. for dedicated capacity we can commit to P95 numbers with an addendum. for hosted, we provide operational metrics and a credit scheme but not a strict latency SLA in the base MSA.
02:08 Leila: that's important. legal will want opt-in language for latency commitments if you plan to include them. also need to see the credit calculation and limitations of liability tied to those credits.
02:25 Ava: from security — we support KMS integrations for key management, data at rest encryption by default, and transport encryption. we maintain audit logs and can provide SOC2 type II report. for private deployments we have options for customer-managed key stores.
02:43 Emily: okay on KMS. do you have an HSM or BYOK flow? we need to know where keys are stored and if redwood can access them.
02:55 Ava: good question. for hosted we offer BYOK via customer KMS and an HSM-backed option with limited access. we don't hold plaintext keys; access controls and RBAC enforced. i'll share the exact architecture diagram after.
03:12 Martin: procurement question — what's the pricing model and approvals? we have a fixed budget line but need committed spend to unlock discounts. we prefer a 12-month committed contract if terms are favorable.
03:28 Jordan: pricing is usage-based for hosted; for dedicated we do reserved capacity pricing with monthly commits. we can model a committed monthly spend to hit your target discounts — priya can run a couple of scenarios in the pilot spreadsheet.
03:40 Priya: i'll put together a benchmark-driven estimate: baseline throughput, expected token volumes, and then show hosted vs dedicated unit economics. we'll include the effect of batching, kv caching, and quantization that redwood supports.
03:55 Rina: from infra side — onboarding: do you need direct network peering or just private link? do you support VPC peering, private link, or on-prem connectors?
04:06 Priya: we support VPC peering and private link for dedicated/private deployments; for hosted we have TLS + IP allowlist and optional private endpoint. for on-prem there is an appliance. we'll attach the onboarding checklist.
04:20 Samir: for the pilot we need a canary path and rollback. do you have canary rollout and traffic split config?
04:30 Priya: yes, we support canary rollouts, route-based ring deploys and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. we'll share a sample rollout config.

06:12 Leila: back to contract terms — indemnity, data retention, and deletion requests. how quickly do you respond to subject access requests?
06:24 Jordan: our standard is comply within statutory periods; for enterprise we can put specific timelines in DPA. we also log data access and can provide audit exports.
06:35 Ava: also note we offer data redaction and controlled retention policies; for regulated customers we can support on-prem deployment so data never leaves their VPC.

10:02 Martin: procurement process and timeline: we'll need legal sign-off, security sign-off, then procurement sends a PO. typical internal lead times are 2-3 weeks once legal and security approve. so target for us is redline complete by Dec 15 to make mid-jan approvals.
10:18 Jordan: that aligns. we'll aim to get redlines back quickly. i'll coordinate with leila and send the MSA + DPA with our suggested edits.

14:05 Leila: a couple of specific asks: 1) can you remove the blanket indemnity for data processing exceptions?, 2) clarify liability caps and carve-outs for gross negligence, 3) add audit rights for a third-party auditor annually.
14:22 Jordan: we'll flag those to legal; our legal team typically discusses carve-outs and can propose compromise language. i'll include our legal counsel on the redline thread.

20:50 Emily: on pen testing and vulnerability disclosure — do you accept coordinated disclosure? do you have an internal cadence for security patching?
21:05 Ava: yes we support coordinated vulnerability disclosure, we run quarterly pentests and weekly patch cycles for infra components. i'll share the most recent pentest summary and the vulnerability response SLA.

28:10 Martin: any competitors in those security docs? procurement wants to compare SOC2 docs side-by-side.
28:20 Jordan: customers often compare us to OpenAI for hosted API and Anthropic for safety, but for enterprise inference runtimes Cohere and some open-source stacks come up. our security pack includes SOC2, pen test, and architecture diagrams for comparison.

34:00 Samir: integration questions — how do you handle model version pinning and rollbacks? we need reproducibility for inference.
34:12 Priya: you can pin model versions in config per route; we support canary model updates and automatic fallback to previous pinned model if quality/regression checks fail. we also support storing eval metadata to tie rollouts to prompt sets.

40:20 Jordan: okay to recap — action items: i'll send the MSA/DPA and an SLA one-pager; priya shares pilot onboarding and benchmark; ava shares SOC2 and KMS docs; martin confirms procurement approvers and timelines. anything missing?
40:40 Martin: pricing — will you please put a committed 12-month and a 3-month pilot option so procurement can evaluate budget impact?
40:52 Priya: yes, we'll include committed vs pilot price scenarios and assumptions.
41:05 Leila: legal will expect a redline by Dec 15, we'll review and come back with consolidated comments.
41:12 Jordan: perfect. we'll aim to meet those dates. thanks all.
41:18 Carlos: i'll follow up with a shared folder link containing documents referenced — MSA, DPA, SLA summary, SOC2, and pilot spreadsheet.
41:28 Rina: one last question on support levels — what are your response times for sev1 incidents under dedicated vs hosted?
41:40 Priya: dedicated includes a priority response SLA (30 minutes initial response for sev1) and a named escalation path; hosted has a 1 hour initial response for sev1 for standard tiers, faster with premium support add-on. we'll include the support table in the one-pager.
41:58 Jordan: great. thanks everyone, we'll send the docs. meeting adjourned.

Closing notes: shared links promised: redwood_msa_v3.pdf (link), redwood_dpa_v2.pdf (link), sla-summary-onepager.pdf (link), pilot-onboarding.xlsx (link), security-pack-soc2.zip (link).
